phase_goal: Every entity from PRD §4 exists in Postgres with Drizzle migrations applied, auth/storage adapters are wired behind their interfaces, and route handlers have the conventions (Zod, Idempotency-Key, cursor pagination, RLS) needed for feature phases to write thin use-cases without reinventing plumbing. Inngest is NOT wired here — it lands in Phase 4 alongside the first async consumer.

prior_decisions: Phase 1 D-07: Path aliases per-root: @contexts/* → src/contexts/*, @shared/* → src/shared/*. No generic @/* alias. Reuse for db/repo files.
Phase 1 D-08: No barrel files. Direct imports only. Continue this rule into the data layer.

Phase 1 D-09: Bounded-context folder tree already shipped — src/contexts/{iam,catalog,species-care,identification,reminders,billing,notifications}/{domain,application,infrastructure,api,inngest}/ + src/shared/{db,events,adapters,config,telemetry}/.
Phase 1 D-10/D-11/D-12: Error registry in src/shared/config/errors.ts as `as const` + literal-union. Error response body is `{ error: { code, message, details? } }`. HTTP mapper helper co-located.
Phase 1 D-25: Postgres 17 everywhere — local Supabase + CI service container. Drizzle migrations run against postgres:17-alpine.
Phase 1 D-29: server-env.ts vs client-env.ts — DATABASE_URL + DATABASE_POOL_URL + SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY live in server-env only; never imported by client modules.

PRD §2 stack: Drizzle ORM (queries inside repositories only), postgres-js + { prepare: false } mandatory for Supavisor txn pooler; route handlers thin (validate → use-case → HTTP map; no Drizzle in handlers).

PRD §5 API rules: JWT per device, opaque cursor pagination (?cursor=&limit=, default 50, max 200, next_cursor in response), Idempotency-Key on mutating endpoints, ISO-8601 UTC timestamps with Z (exception: User.notification_time_local is HH:MM in User.timezone), closed error registry including validation_failed, conflict, unauthenticated.

PRD §11 image pipeline: client-side compression to ≤1MB + EXIF/GPS strip → upload → server rejects GPS-bearing as validation_failed → thumbnail generation → originals preserved. Failure modes: retry once at lower quality; upload mid-fail stays in IndexedDB queue; thumbnail-gen fail keeps original + placeholder + later regen.
PRD §13 LGPD: ConsentLog with policy_version + legal_basis registry (contract, consent, legitimate_interest); Art. 33 international transfer consent before Plant.id/OpenAI-compat call.
PRD §3 bounded-context emission map: who emits/consumes which events. Phase 2 is NOT wiring Inngest, but the cross-context contract is locked.
PRD §4 entity field shapes: 19 entities with their columns are spec'd; the question for Phase 2 is HOW to express them in Drizzle, not WHAT they are.
Storage buckets: plant-photos, plant-thumbnails, data-exports — all PRIVATE (signed-URL only).
Inngest: NOT in Phase 2 (lands Phase 4 with verification email as first async consumer). Event publishing infrastructure decision still possibly relevant (defining types vs not).

questions.title: Drizzle schema file layout
questions.context: Repo already has src/contexts/{iam,catalog,...}/infrastructure/ ready and src/shared/db/ as a shared root. Drizzle wants to enumerate every table for migration generation. Choice trades context-ownership purity vs. cross-aggregate FK ergonomics.

options.label: Per-context schemas + shared barrel for drizzle-kit
options.description: Each context owns src/contexts/{ctx}/infrastructure/db/schema.ts for its aggregates; src/shared/db/schema.ts re-exports them so drizzle-kit sees one entry point. Best DDD alignment. FK across contexts requires importing across modules.

options.label: Centralized schema in src/shared/db/schema.ts
options.description: Single file with all 19 entities. FK across contexts trivial. Bounded-context separation lives only in repository placement, not schema files. Smallest moving parts.

options.label: Per-aggregate files in src/shared/db/schemas/
options.description: One file per entity (user.ts, plant.ts, ...) imported from src/shared/db/schema.ts barrel. Easier diffs, no per-context boundary. Hybrid — keeps schema centralized but file-grained.

questions.chat_more: The shared file should be treated as src/shared/db/schema-registry.ts for drizzle-kit only, not an application import barrel. Add a lint/test guard if needed.

questions.title: Primary key strategy
questions.context: PRD §4 lists `id` on every entity but doesn't lock the type. Choice affects URL safety, index size, sort behavior, dependency footprint, and whether IDs leak count.

options.label: UUID v4 (PG `gen_random_uuid()`)
options.description: Postgres-native (pgcrypto), 128-bit, opaque, no extra dep, no sort signal. Universally portable. Slight index bloat vs sequential.

options.label: UUID v7 (time-sortable, app-side)
options.description: 128-bit, monotonic prefix → better B-tree locality, better range queries on `created_at` proxy. Needs `uuid` v9+ npm dep generated app-side (PG 17 has no native v7 yet).

options.label: bigserial (sequential int8)
options.description: Smallest indexes, fastest joins. Exposes row count in URLs (privacy + competitive concern), trivial enumeration. Non-portable across shards.

options.label: cuid2 (collision-resistant, short)
options.description: Short, secure, sortable-ish. Adds @paralleldrive/cuid2 dep. Less common in Postgres ecosystems; debugging tools less aware.

questions.title: Timestamp columns & defaults
questions.context: PRD §5 locks ISO-8601 UTC with `Z` for all timestamps. Decision is about column type (timestamptz vs timestamp), default-value source (DB clock vs app clock), and naming (snake_case in DB).

options.label: timestamptz + PG `now()` defaults + snake_case (`created_at`, `updated_at`)
options.description: Postgres handles UTC normalization, drizzle-kit emits `DEFAULT now()`. Writes don't need to set `created_at`. Matches Postgres convention.

options.label: timestamptz + app-side timestamps (no PG defaults)
options.description: App generates `new Date()` and inserts explicitly. Easier to mock/freeze in tests, deterministic. Slightly more code per insert.

options.label: timestamp (no tz) + UTC convention enforced in app
options.description: Smallest column. Loses timezone info entirely; relies on every consumer assuming UTC. Brittle if anyone forgets.

questions.title: Enum strategy for status/type fields
questions.context: PRD §4 has many enum-shaped fields: `Identification.status (success|failed)`, `Identification.failure_reason (timeout|provider_unavailable|cost_ceiling_reached|breaker_open|invalid_response)`, `Subscription.status (trialing|active|past_due|canceled|expired)`, `Reminder.type (watering|fertilization)`, `CareGuide.toxicity (safe|toxic_pets|toxic_children|toxic_both)`, etc. Choice trades schema strictness vs migration flexibility.

options.label: Postgres native ENUMs via `pgEnum` (drizzle helper)
options.description: DB-enforced, type-safe, `\d+` shows the values. Adding a new value needs `ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE` (cannot run inside transactions in older PG; PG 17 allows). Removing a value requires recreating the type.

options.label: varchar + CHECK constraint + TS literal union
options.description: Drizzle column is `varchar` with a CHECK; TS layer has `type Status = 'trialing' | 'active' | ...`. Adding values = relaxing the CHECK in a migration. Removing = harder. Less DB-side introspection.

options.label: varchar + TS validation only (Zod literal union, no DB CHECK)
options.description: Most flexible. Zod at the route boundary is the only enforcement. DB accepts any string — risk of bad data from manual SQL or admin scripts.

questions.title: Column naming convention
questions.context: PRD §4 uses snake_case (`user_id`, `acquisition_date`, `current_period_end`). TypeScript convention is camelCase. Drizzle supports either with mapping, but consistency matters.

options.label: snake_case columns ↔ camelCase TS via Drizzle mapping
options.description: DB stays Postgres-idiomatic (`user_id`, `created_at`); TS reads `userId`, `createdAt`. Best for SQL admins + ORM users. Drizzle handles via `name: 'user_id'`.

options.label: camelCase columns + camelCase TS (uniform everywhere)
options.description: Drizzle just uses the field name as the column name. SQL queries quote `"userId"` (case-sensitive). Less idiomatic in Postgres tooling.

options.label: snake_case columns + snake_case TS
options.description: Match DB names verbatim. Unusual for TS code but eliminates a class of mapping bugs. Reads less idiomatically in JS land.

questions.title: JSON column type for opaque payloads
questions.context: Three entities carry JSON: `Identification.results` (top-N w/ confidence — sometimes queried by status/min_confidence at insert), `BillingEvent.payload` (raw Stripe event), `OfflineSyncFailure.payload` (queued action). PG 17 has both `json` (preserves raw text) and `jsonb` (parsed binary, indexable).

options.label: jsonb everywhere
options.description: Indexable, faster random reads, lossy on whitespace. Industry default for new projects.

options.label: json everywhere
options.description: Preserves exact bytes (good for webhook signature verification audits). Faster writes, no indexability. Useful if BillingEvent.payload needs byte-faithful retention.

options.label: Mixed — jsonb for queryable fields, json for opaque payloads
options.description: `Identification.results` = jsonb (we may filter on confidence in admin queries); `BillingEvent.payload` + `OfflineSyncFailure.payload` = json (audit-faithful).

questions.title: Cross-aggregate FK constraints
questions.context: Plant.user_id → User.id, Plant.species_id → Species.id (nullable), PhotoEntry.plant_id → Plant.id, Identification.user_id → User.id, Identification.plant_id → Plant.id (set NULL on plant delete per PRD §4), etc. Real DB FKs catch bugs early but make migrations heavier.

options.label: Real FKs everywhere with explicit ON DELETE rules per PRD §4
options.description: CASCADE for ownership (PhotoEntry.plant_id, Reminder.plant_id), SET NULL for cross-context history (Identification.plant_id), RESTRICT/NO ACTION for reference (Plant.species_id). Maximum referential integrity.

options.label: Real FKs with default ON DELETE NO ACTION + app-level cascade logic
options.description: DB enforces existence; deletion semantics live in repositories/use-cases (more visible in code, easier to test). Risk: double-delete if app and DB both attempt cascade.

options.label: No DB FKs, app-level integrity only
options.description: Allows independent context schema migrations. Big consistency risk — easy to leak orphans. Drizzle still has TS-level relations for joins.

questions.title: Migration directory ownership
questions.context: Two systems can own migrations: drizzle-kit (TS-driven, generates SQL from schema diffs) and Supabase CLI (`supabase/migrations/*.sql`, runs on `db reset`, also handles RLS/storage). Locally, `db:reset` is in package.json from Phase 1. Choice impacts where SQL lives + who runs it.

options.label: drizzle-kit owns ALL migrations in `drizzle/migrations/`
options.description: Supabase CLI is just for local services (Postgres + Auth + Storage). Drizzle migrations applied via `pnpm db:migrate` or pre-test hook. RLS is also drizzle-kit (raw SQL embedded). One source of truth, `supabase db reset` doesn't auto-run them — needs custom orchestration.

options.label: drizzle-kit generates SQL → output to `supabase/migrations/`
options.description: Supabase CLI's `db reset` picks them up automatically. Lose drizzle-kit's `migrate` command but gain Supabase CLI's diff-and-deploy + branch-DB story. Naming conventions need to align (`YYYYMMDDHHMMSS_description.sql`).

options.label: Two systems — drizzle-kit for app schema, supabase/migrations for RLS + storage policies + seeding triggers
options.description: Each tool owns its strength. Risk: ordering bugs (RLS migration runs before table exists). Need clear sequencing convention.

questions.title: Migration application strategy
questions.context: drizzle-kit offers `push` (introspect + apply schema directly, no migration file) vs `generate` (write SQL file from schema diff) + `migrate` (apply checked-in files). Phase 2 SC-1 says migrations are applied to a fresh DB, implying file-based.

options.label: `drizzle-kit generate` + checked-in SQL + `drizzle-kit migrate`
options.description: Migration files in repo, full audit trail, prod-style. CI applies the same files as dev. Slight friction during early-phase schema iteration (regenerate often).

options.label: `drizzle-kit push` (no migration files)
options.description: Schema-direct sync, fast iteration, zero file noise. NO audit trail — any out-of-band change to prod overwrites silently. Only safe for greenfield local dev.

options.label: Hybrid — `push` in local dev, `generate+migrate` in CI/preview/prod
options.description: Best of both. Risk: drift between dev (push'd schema) and migration files. Need a `db:migrate-check` script that asserts they match.

questions.title: RLS policy authoring location
questions.context: RLS policies are SQL — `CREATE POLICY ... ON tablename FOR SELECT USING (auth.uid() = user_id)`. They're tightly coupled to the schema (same table, same migration moment). Where to keep them?

options.label: Embedded in same drizzle migration files via raw SQL strings
options.description: drizzle-kit emits CREATE TABLE; we hand-edit (or hook drizzle's `customMigration`) to append CREATE POLICY. Single migration file = single source of truth for that table.

options.label: Separate `supabase/migrations/*-rls.sql` files post-table
options.description: Hand-authored, run after drizzle migrations. Clear separation: "schema vs policy". Risk: mismatch if a column name changes and the RLS file doesn't.

options.label: Drizzle's declarative RLS API (limited) + raw SQL for the rest
options.description: Drizzle 0.45 has experimental `pgPolicy()` for simple cases. Use it when possible, raw SQL fallback for `auth.uid()`-dependent policies. Most modern; less mature.

questions.title: Migration verification in CI
questions.context: Phase 2 SC-1 requires migrations apply to a fresh DB cleanly. CI integration tests need migrations + seed before tests run. Failure to verify could let drift land.

options.label: CI pre-test step: `db:reset` → `db:migrate` → `db:seed` → run tests
options.description: Three-step orchestration. Each piece is independently runnable. Slow if seed is large.

options.label: CI pre-test step: `db:setup` (single command) → run tests
options.description: Wrapper script does reset + migrate + seed in one shot. Less granular but easier to invoke.

options.label: Per-test-file fresh DB (slower but safer)
options.description: Each Vitest worker spins up its own DB or schema. Eliminates cross-test pollution. Significantly slower CI.

questions.title: Seed data format
questions.context: INFRA-24 requires ConsentLog policy_version + legal-basis registry seeded everywhere. Plus: IdentificationLimit defaults (trial/paid caps), ProviderBudget defaults ($5/day each, alert 80%, min_confidence 0.30). Choice affects type-safety and refactor cost.

options.label: `supabase/seed.sql` (raw SQL, run by `db:reset`)
options.description: Supabase CLI handles it natively. Static data, easy to review in PR. No type-safety — column rename breaks silently until next reset.

options.label: TS-based seed runner — `scripts/seed.ts` via `tsx`, uses Drizzle insert helpers
options.description: Type-safe (column rename → compile error). Refactor-friendly. Needs explicit `pnpm db:seed` invocation (or hook into `db:reset` via supabase config). Harder to run in CI without Node.

options.label: Mixed — SQL for static reference (legal-basis, defaults), TS for dev fixtures (test users, plants)
options.description: Static immutable data via SQL (audit-friendly), dev-only convenience via TS. Two sources, but each is appropriate to its scope.

questions.title: Seed coverage at Phase 2
questions.context: Phase 2 SC-5 only requires ConsentLog policy_version + legal-basis registry. PRD also has IdentificationLimit + ProviderBudget defaults. Anything else seeded now is Phase 5+ scaffolding.

options.label: Minimum required: ConsentLog policy_version + legal-basis registry only
options.description: Strict to SC-5. IdentificationLimit + ProviderBudget seeded by Phase 6 when caps actually engage.

options.label: Above + IdentificationLimit (trial 5/75, paid 15/200) + ProviderBudget defaults ($5/day Plant.id + OpenAI-compat, 80% alert, min_confidence 0.30)
options.description: Phase 6 needs them; landing in Phase 2 means a fresh DB is always identification-ready (if connected to a provider). Aligns with PRD §6 cost-control table.

options.label: Above + sample PartnerStore rows (e.g., `internal-test` partner code) for E2E
options.description: Phase 4 needs partner codes for signup. Seeding now means E2E in Phase 4 doesn't need its own setup.

options.label: Above + sample test users + test plants (dev-only, not loaded in prod)
options.description: Convenient for dev/manual testing. Risk of leaking into prod if seed file isn't gated by NODE_ENV.

questions.title: Pooled vs direct connection separation
questions.context: App runs on Vercel serverless → goes through Supavisor txn pooler at port 6543 with `prepare: false`. drizzle-kit migrations + admin scripts use direct DB connection at port 5432 (txn pooler doesn't allow DDL). DATABASE_URL + DATABASE_POOL_URL already in .env per Phase 1.

options.label: Two clients — `db/client.ts` (pooled, `{ prepare: false }`) for app; `db/migration-client.ts` (direct) for drizzle-kit + scripts
options.description: Clean separation. App never touches direct connection (production safety). drizzle-kit gets its own narrow file.

options.label: Single client (pooled, `{ prepare: false }`) used everywhere
options.description: Simpler. drizzle-kit migrations might fail (txn pooler rejects DDL). Risk: production DDL from app accidentally.

questions.title: Client lifecycle in Next 16 serverless
questions.context: Vercel functions can warm up/cool down. postgres-js opens TCP connections. Connection pooling is at Supavisor — local pool size matters mostly for hot-reload safety in dev.

options.label: Single global lazy-initialized client (module-scope)
options.description: Standard serverless pattern. Postgres connection persists across warm invocations. Hot-reload in dev creates leaks until process restart — acceptable.

options.label: Lazy global + explicit `db.end()` on hot-reload (dev-only HMR hook)
options.description: Add a Vite/Next HMR hook to close connections on module replacement. Cleaner dev DX, more code.

options.label: Per-request client instantiation
options.description: Fresh client per request, explicit close at end. Burns connection budget; safest cleanup. Likely overkill with Supavisor in front.

questions.title: Repository style (DDD strictness)
questions.context: Folhário's PROJECT.md emphasizes "adapter boundaries at every external dependency" + "DDD-lite per bounded context". Repositories abstract DB access from use-cases. Choice trades testability/swappability against ceremony.

options.label: DDD strict — interface in `domain/{aggregate}-repository.ts`, impl in `infrastructure/{aggregate}-repository.drizzle.ts`
options.description: Use-cases depend on interface. Mockable for unit tests. Maximum boilerplate. Easy to add an in-memory test impl.

options.label: Concrete only — `infrastructure/{aggregate}-repository.ts` exporting class or instance
options.description: No domain-layer interface. Pragmatic. Use-cases depend on the class directly. Mocking requires `vi.mock` or DI param. Less code.

options.label: Functional — `infrastructure/db/{aggregate}.ts` exporting `findById`, `create`, etc. (no class, no `this`)
options.description: Pure functions take a Drizzle client param. Easiest to test. No DDD-style "object identity". Very TS-idiomatic.

questions.title: How to enforce "no Drizzle in handlers"
questions.context: Phase 2 SC-2 says "integration tests fail loudly if any route handler imports Drizzle directly". CLAUDE.md and PROJECT.md repeat the rule. Mechanism choice trades author-time vs. test-time enforcement.

options.label: ESLint `no-restricted-imports` rule on `src/app/api/**`
options.description: Forbid `drizzle-orm`, `drizzle-orm/postgres-js`, and `@shared/db/client` from being imported by route handler files. Lint failure on commit/CI. Author sees error in editor.

options.label: Vitest test that greps `src/app/api/` for forbidden imports
options.description: Runtime test in CI. Catches all variants of import (require, dynamic). Slower feedback than lint but harder to disable.

options.label: Both — ESLint + Vitest grep test (belt and suspenders)
options.description: ESLint for fast author feedback, Vitest for CI safety net. Slight duplication.

questions.title: Transaction API exposure
questions.context: Use-cases sometimes need atomic multi-table writes (e.g., create Plant + initial PhotoEntry). Drizzle exposes `db.transaction(async (tx) => ...)`. Repositories must accept the tx context.

options.label: Repositories take optional `tx?: Drizzle` parameter on every method
options.description: `async create(data, tx?: Tx)` — tx defaults to global db. Use-cases call `db.transaction((tx) => repo.create(data, tx))`. Pragmatic, type-safe, slightly leaky.

options.label: Repositories expose `withTx(tx)` factory returning a tx-bound repo
options.description: `const txRepo = repo.withTx(tx)`. Cleaner — methods don't carry tx param. More code in repos.

options.label: Unit-of-Work abstraction hiding Drizzle entirely
options.description: `uow.execute(async (uow) => uow.plants.create(data))`. Most DDD-pure. Highest ceremony. Hardest to read for casual contributors.

questions.title: drizzle-zod usage pattern
questions.context: INFRA-09 says "Zod validation at route-handler body/query boundaries; drizzle-zod for DB-schema-derived Zod". drizzle-zod gives `createInsertSchema` + `createSelectSchema` — but raw schemas often need pt-BR error messages and business rules layered on.

options.label: Routes import `createInsertSchema(plants)` directly
options.description: Minimal layer. Fastest. pt-BR error messages must be added at schema definition or via Zod's `errorMap` globally. Thin route handler.

options.label: Domain layer exports refined Zod schemas
options.description: `src/contexts/catalog/domain/plant-schemas.ts` extends `createInsertSchema` with pt-BR messages, business rules (`name.min(1).max(80)`). Routes import from domain. More files but separates concerns.

options.label: Two layers — raw drizzle-zod for shape + composed domain Zod for rules
options.description: Domain composes raw + business rules. Routes always import domain version. Most explicit, most files.

questions.title: Auth model for RLS
questions.context: PRD §2 says "RLS as defense in depth". The app primarily uses service-role key (server-only, bypasses RLS). RLS only kicks in if someone authenticates as a user via JWT. Two patterns exist: (1) Supabase pattern — every request opens a JWT-bearing PG connection, RLS enforces user_id filtering automatically; (2) Service-role + app-level WHERE filters — RLS exists only as a backstop.

options.label: Service-role + app-level `WHERE user_id = ?` in every repo (RLS strictly defense-in-depth)
options.description: Repos always filter by user_id explicitly. Simple connection model (one client, service role). RLS is a backstop if a repo forgets the filter. Most testable. Aligns with current Drizzle patterns.

options.label: Per-request JWT-bearing PG connection (RLS is primary enforcement)
options.description: Each `/api/v1/*` request creates a Drizzle client with the user's JWT in `Authorization` header → Supavisor passes through → `auth.uid()` works in policies → repos skip explicit user_id filter. Fewer bugs, harder to test.

options.label: Hybrid — service-role for cross-context reads (Species, CareGuide, partner stores) + JWT-bearing for user-scoped mutations
options.description: Best of both. Two clients per request worst-case. Most code paths to think about.

questions.title: Which tables get RLS enabled
questions.context: User-owned (need RLS): User, Plant, PhotoEntry, Reminder, ReminderLog, Identification, ConsentLog, DataExportRequest, DataDeletionRequest, Subscription, OfflineSyncFailure, PushSubscription. Reference/admin: Species, CareGuide, PartnerStore, IdentificationLimit, ProviderBudget, ProviderUsageCounter, BillingEvent.

options.label: RLS on all 12 user-owned tables; reference/admin tables have RLS disabled
options.description: Strict to PRD wording "all user-owned tables". Minimum surface. Reference tables stay unrestricted at DB level (service role enforces).

options.label: RLS enabled on ALL tables; reference tables have permissive `FOR SELECT TO authenticated USING (true)` policies
options.description: Uniform posture: every table has RLS on. Reference tables explicitly grant read. Most defense. Slight policy bloat.

options.label: RLS on user-owned + RLS on reference tables (read-only via authenticated role) + admin tables RLS-off
options.description: Species/CareGuide can be read by anyone authenticated; IdentificationLimit/ProviderBudget operator-tunable via service role only. Most expressive.

questions.title: RLS policy granularity
questions.context: PG supports `FOR ALL` (combined SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE) and per-action policies. Decision affects audit complexity vs explicit semantics.

options.label: Single `FOR ALL` policy per user-owned table — `USING (auth.uid() = user_id) WITH CHECK (auth.uid() = user_id)`
options.description: Minimum policy lines. Same condition for read/write. Simplest mental model.

options.label: Separate SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE policies per table
options.description: Explicit per-action enforcement. Easier to audit what each operation requires. More lines.

options.label: Mixed — `FOR ALL` for symmetric cases, separate policies where rules differ (e.g., SELECT permissive for Species but INSERT operator-only)
options.description: Pragmatic — granularity scales with table needs. Most expressive.

questions.title: RLS on storage buckets (`plant-photos`, `plant-thumbnails`, `data-exports`)
questions.context: Buckets are private. Two enforcement layers exist: (1) Supabase Storage bucket-level RLS via `storage.objects` policies referencing `auth.uid()` and path; (2) Server proxy — clients never touch buckets directly, server uses service role + signed URLs.

options.label: Path-based bucket RLS — `(storage.foldername(name))[1] = auth.uid()::text` policy
options.description: Path convention `{user_id}/...` enforced at storage layer. Direct client uploads possible (signed-upload-URL). RLS is the gate.

options.label: Service-role only — clients never call Supabase Storage directly
options.description: Server proxies uploads via service role; clients receive signed download URLs. Maximum control (we can validate GPS, transform, gate by subscription). Adds server bandwidth on uploads.

options.label: Both — path-based RLS for direct uploads (after signed-upload-URL grant) + signed URLs for downloads + server-side GPS check on upload notification
options.description: Direct client → bucket via signed URL (fast, low server bandwidth) + server validates the EXIF via post-upload Supabase storage event/Inngest hook. Inngest deferred to Phase 4 — would need a sync alternative now.

questions.title: Bucket provisioning mechanism
questions.context: Three private buckets need to exist in every environment: `plant-photos`, `plant-thumbnails`, `data-exports`. Supabase CLI's config.toml has `[storage.buckets.<name>]` declarative blocks; raw SQL works too.

options.label: `supabase/config.toml` declarative `[storage.buckets.*]` blocks
options.description: Supabase CLI creates buckets on `supabase start` / `db reset`. Schema-coupled to migrations. Per-bucket settings (public, file_size_limit, allowed_mime_types) declarative.

options.label: SQL migration that inserts into `storage.buckets`
options.description: Lives alongside other migrations. Works in any environment. Slightly more brittle — Supabase Storage internal table format may change.

options.label: TS setup script `scripts/setup-buckets.ts` using Supabase JS admin API
options.description: Idempotent creation via Supabase JS client. Easy to run against any environment with credentials. Extra moving piece — must be invoked manually.

questions.title: StorageAdapter interface granularity
questions.context: INFRA-06 mandates `StorageAdapter` with signed-URL helpers. Decision: how abstract is the API surface?

options.label: High-level — `uploadPlantPhoto(userId, plantId, buffer): { photoUrl, thumbnailUrl }`, `uploadDataExport(userId, archive)`, etc.
options.description: Encapsulates path + bucket per use-case. Use-cases stay clean. Adapter has many methods. Path conventions live inside adapter.

options.label: Low-level — `upload(bucket, path, file)`, `getSignedUrl(bucket, path, ttl)`, `delete(bucket, path)`
options.description: Generic. Callers compose paths. Adapter has 3-4 methods. Path conventions live in callers (or in a `paths.ts` helper).

options.label: Two-tier — low-level adapter `StorageAdapter` + high-level helpers per context (`src/contexts/catalog/infrastructure/photo-storage.ts`)
options.description: Adapter is generic, swappable. Per-context helpers wrap with path conventions. Cleanest layering, more files.

questions.title: Storage path convention
questions.context: Bucket layout affects RLS (path-based policies), LGPD per-user delete (rm -rf {user_id}/), debugging, and future migrations.

options.label: `{user_id}/{aggregate_id}/{file_id}.{ext}` — e.g., `plant-photos/abc-123/plant-789/photo-xyz.jpg`
options.description: Easy LGPD delete (drop prefix). Easy RLS via foldername(name). Aggregate-grouped listings. Clear lineage.

options.label: `{user_id}/{file_id}.{ext}` — flat per user
options.description: Simpler. No aggregate grouping; aggregate id lives only in DB. Easy LGPD. Slight risk of file-id collisions (mitigated by UUIDs).

options.label: `{user_id}/{yyyy-mm}/{file_id}.{ext}` — month-sharded
options.description: Better for backup/archive workflows. More complex prefix logic. Harder to find files by aggregate.

questions.title: Upload mechanism
questions.context: Two patterns for Supabase Storage uploads: (1) Client → server route → service-role upload; (2) Client → server gets signed-upload-URL → client direct uploads → server records metadata. EXIF/GPS checks must happen somewhere.

options.label: Server proxy — client POSTs multipart to `/api/v1/photos/upload`, server runs GPS check, server uploads via service role, server inserts DB row
options.description: Single atomic transaction (file uploaded ↔ DB row exists). GPS check at server boundary (defense in depth). Burns server bandwidth on uploads — every byte hits Vercel.

options.label: Direct upload via signed URL — server returns signed-upload-URL, client uploads to Supabase, server callback inserts DB row
options.description: Minimal server bandwidth. GPS check requires post-upload validation (server fetches just EXIF and validates) → risk of orphaned files if check fails. Needs cleanup logic.

options.label: Hybrid — direct upload via signed URL + server post-upload GPS validation in same request flow
options.description: Client uploads to Supabase, then POSTs metadata + checksum to `/api/v1/photos/confirm`. Server fetches EXIF (lightweight HEAD/range read), rejects + deletes object if GPS present, otherwise inserts DB row. More moving parts.

questions.title: Client-side compression library
questions.context: PRD §11: client-side compression to ≤1MB. Choice affects bundle size, EXIF strip behavior, browser support, and developer ergonomics.

options.label: `browser-image-compression` (popular, ~5k stars)
options.description: Battle-tested, supports EXIF strip option, async API, configurable target size. Bundle ~30KB gzipped. Workers support.

options.label: `compressorjs` (lighter, jQuery-style API)
options.description: Smaller bundle (~12KB). Less rich API. Doesn't strip EXIF natively — needs separate piexifjs.

options.label: Custom Canvas API (`canvas.toBlob({ quality })`)
options.description: Zero deps. Implements iterative quality downsampling manually. Strips EXIF as side effect of canvas redraw. Most code, most control.

questions.title: EXIF strip approach (client-side)
questions.context: Even with compression, EXIF survival depends on the library. PRD §11 mandates client strips EXIF including GPS before upload.

options.label: Bundled in compression library (browser-image-compression has `exifOrientation` + strip options)
options.description: Single dep. Library guarantees no EXIF in output. Implicit — easy to forget to enable.

options.label: Separate `piexifjs` after compression
options.description: Explicit two-step: compress → piexifjs.remove(). Verifiable in tests. Two deps. Slight bundle bloat.

options.label: Canvas redraw guarantees no EXIF (option Q-28-c)
options.description: If we go with custom Canvas, EXIF is gone by construction (canvas can't re-emit it). Implicit but provably correct.

questions.title: Server-side GPS detection library
questions.context: PRD §11 server defense in depth: "server REJECTS uploads still carrying GPS as `validation_failed`". Server must read EXIF without trusting the client.

options.label: `exifr` (light, modern, ESM)
options.description: Fast (parses streams), small (~10KB), works in Node + browser. Supports JPEG/HEIC/TIFF. Most maintained option in 2026.

options.label: `exiftool-vendored` (full ExifTool wrapper)
options.description: Comprehensive (handles every format). Bundles a Perl runtime + binary. Heavy (50MB+) — bad for serverless cold start.

options.label: `piexifjs` (small, JPEG-only)
options.description: Lightweight, works in Node. JPEG-only — fails on HEIC (iOS default). Risky if iOS users upload from Camera Roll.

questions.title: Thumbnail generation timing
questions.context: PRD §11 mandates thumbnails. Phase 5 (Catalog) is the first consumer. Generation could happen sync (Sharp on server upload), async (Inngest function — but Inngest doesn't land until Phase 4), or via Supabase image transformations.

options.label: Sync in upload route — `sharp` resizes + uploads thumbnail to `plant-thumbnails` in same request
options.description: Atomic. Latency: resize 200-400ms per photo. Sharp adds ~10MB to bundle (native binary). Phase 2 ships fully.

options.label: Supabase image transformations (`?width=300` query)
options.description: No thumbnails bucket needed. Edge-cached. Fees per transformation. May not match "plant-thumbnails bucket" scoping in INFRA-06.

options.label: Defer thumbnail generation logic to Phase 5 — Phase 2 only ships the bucket + adapter scaffolding
options.description: Phase 2 SC-3 only requires buckets boot without errors. Thumbnail generation is INFRA-19 which doesn't strictly require Phase 2. Move to Phase 5 (catalog) where it's first needed. Honest scope.

options.label: Async Inngest function — but Inngest doesn't exist yet (Phase 4)
options.description: Would defer Phase 2 scope. Not viable now without breaking phase ordering.

questions.title: AuthAdapter scope at Phase 2
questions.context: Phase 4 owns full auth (signup, OAuth, verification, reset). Phase 2 SC-4 says "enforces JWT verification via Next middleware". Question: how thin is the AuthAdapter at Phase 2?

options.label: Thin — only `verifyJWT(token) → { userId, email, ... }` exposed
options.description: Phase 2 ships JWT verification, nothing else. Phase 4 adds signup/signin/reset to the same adapter. Minimum surface.

options.label: Skeleton — verify + stubbed signUp/signIn/requestReset that throw "not implemented"
options.description: Adapter interface defined upfront. Phase 4 fills in. Clearer contract earlier; nothing usable yet.

options.label: Verify + `getUserById(id)` (small DB read used by smoke route + Phase 5+ catalog)
options.description: Just enough to power the Phase 2 smoke endpoint that asserts "the authenticated user has a User row". Practical minimum for downstream phases.

questions.title: JWT verification mechanism
questions.context: Supabase signs JWTs with a project secret (or via JWKS). Verification options trade SDK weight vs control.

options.label: `jose` library + JWKS endpoint (`{SUPABASE_URL}/auth/v1/.well-known/jwks.json`)
options.description: Tiny dep, full control, async-friendly. Caches JWKS. Best for serverless cold start.

options.label: `@supabase/supabase-js` server client with `auth.getUser()`
options.description: Bundles auth + DB + storage clients. Heaviest. Goes well beyond verify-only — drags in JS-land patterns we don't need at the data-layer phase.

options.label: `@supabase/ssr` (Next-aware, cookie-based)
options.description: Designed for Server Components/Actions. Uses cookies. Phase 2 is mostly route handlers (Bearer tokens), so SSR-cookie semantics may not fit.

questions.title: Middleware location for JWT verification
questions.context: Phase 1 D-24 puts security headers in `next.config.ts headers()` and locale routing in `src/proxy.ts` (next-intl). JWT verification is a third concern. Where does it live?

options.label: Extend `src/proxy.ts` with auth check after locale handling
options.description: Single proxy file, conditional matchers. Re-uses Next 16 proxy/middleware infrastructure already wired. Mixed concerns.

options.label: Compose two functions in `src/proxy.ts` (locale + auth) via runtime helper
options.description: `export default chain([locale, auth])` — cleaner separation, both run in one file. Custom chaining helper.

options.label: Per-route validation via shared helper (`requireAuth(req)`) in route handlers — no middleware
options.description: Each route handler calls `await requireAuth(req)` at top. Explicit, auditable. Repetitive. Risk: missing on a new route.

questions.title: User row sync (Supabase `auth.users` ↔ `public.users`)
questions.context: Supabase Auth lives in its own `auth.users` table. Folhário's `User` lives in `public.users` (with extra fields: timezone, notification_time_local, trial_source, etc.). When a JWT arrives, the public.users row may not exist yet.

options.label: DB trigger on `auth.users` INSERT → INSERT INTO `public.users` with defaults; app fills extra fields later
options.description: Atomic with auth signup. Extra fields (timezone, notification_time_local) defaulted; app updates them on first authed request or Phase 4 signup endpoint. Trigger lives in supabase/migrations.

options.label: App-side lazy create — first authed request without a User row creates it
options.description: No trigger needed. Race condition possible if two requests arrive concurrently for the same auth.user. Mitigate with `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`.

options.label: Defer entirely to Phase 4 — Phase 2 ships the User table + AuthAdapter but no sync logic
options.description: Phase 2 smoke route accepts "user has no public.users row → 401 user_not_provisioned" or similar. Phase 4 signup endpoint creates the row explicitly.

questions.title: Cursor encoding format
questions.context: PRD §5: "opaque cursor, `?cursor=&limit=` (default 50, max 200), response carries `next_cursor` (null when exhausted). Clients MUST NOT parse cursors." Implementation choice trades simplicity vs tamper-resistance.

options.label: `base64(JSON.stringify({ id, createdAt }))`
options.description: Simple, opaque enough. Tampering yields 400 (invalid JSON or out-of-range data). Easy to debug in dev (decode in console).

options.label: HMAC-signed cursor with secret from env
options.description: Tamper-proof. Slight code overhead (sign + verify). Harder to debug. Overkill for IDs that are already opaque (UUIDs).

options.label: Plain composite — `{lastId}_{lastSortKey}` as a string
options.description: No encoding. Visibly tied to ORDER BY column. Easier to reason about. Exposes internal column names slightly.

questions.title: Idempotency-Key implementation
questions.context: INFRA-22: Idempotency-Key on mutating endpoints; client UUID is the key for offline queue actions. Implementation determines TTL, replay semantics, and storage.

options.label: `IdempotencyKey` table (key, user_id, response_status, response_body, expires_at)
options.description: DB-backed. Survives restarts. Race-safe via unique constraint. Replay returns the persisted response. Adds writes to every mutation. Easy to reason about.

options.label: Postgres advisory locks keyed on `hash(key)` — no extra table
options.description: Briefly locks on concurrent replays. Replay returns "in progress" or completed result. Less storage. Lock release on connection close — risk of stuck locks.

options.label: In-memory LRU per server instance
options.description: Fastest. Useless across serverless invocations (no shared state). Effectively means only same-instance dedup — usually accidental.

questions.title: Idempotency-Key TTL
questions.context: Offline-queue replays can arrive long after original (LGPD grace = 7d, app might be offline for days). Too short = duplicate work; too long = unbounded table growth.

options.label: 24 hours uniform
options.description: Typical mobile-offline replay window. Most queued actions reach server within a day.

options.label: 7 days uniform
options.description: Matches LGPD deletion grace + Inngest free-tier `sleepUntil` cap. Safer for long offline streaks. More table growth.

options.label: 48 hours uniform
options.description: Generous for offline-queue replay; limits unbounded growth. Middle ground.

questions.title: Smoke endpoint subject for SC-4
questions.context: Phase 2 SC-4 says: "A smoke `/api/v1/*` route handler validates body with drizzle-zod-derived Zod, enforces JWT verification via Next middleware, returns cursor-paginated responses, and dedupes POSTs by Idempotency-Key header." Need a concrete subject that exercises all four.

options.label: Pure read smoke — `GET /api/v1/health/db?cursor=&limit=` returning paginated empty `users` slice (operator-only)
options.description: Touches DB via repo (proves client + repo layer wire). Read-only — doesn't exercise idempotency or Zod validation.

options.label: ConsentLog write smoke — `POST /api/v1/_diagnostics/consent` records ConsentLog row, requires Idempotency-Key, returns paginated GET history
options.description: Exercises every requirement (Zod insert validation + JWT + cursor on GET + Idempotency on POST). ConsentLog is real data needed by Phase 4. Real product surface, audit-friendly.

options.label: Diagnostic-only `/api/v1/_diagnostics/probe` against a throwaway `Probe` entity (CI/preview-only)
options.description: Doesn't touch real product tables. Cleanly removable post-Phase-2. Adds entity that exists only for testing.

options.label: All three — `/health/db` + ConsentLog write + cursor probe
options.description: Belt-and-suspenders coverage. Most code, most surface. Each piece justifiable.

questions.title: Domain entity layer style
questions.context: DDD-classic has rich domain classes with invariants and methods. Lean approach uses Zod-derived types only. Functional uses ADTs + helpers. PROJECT.md says "DDD-lite per bounded context" but doesn't specify class vs function.

options.label: Lean — types derived from drizzle-zod (`type Plant = z.infer<typeof selectPlantSchema>`), no class layer
options.description: Minimum ceremony. Use-cases are functions taking/returning types. Easy onboarding. "DDD-lite" interpreted loosely.

options.label: DDD-classic — domain classes per aggregate (`class Plant { rename(name) { ... } }`) with invariants
options.description: Maximum DDD. Domain-method-driven mutations. Repos hydrate/persist instances. Highest ceremony; highest expressiveness.

options.label: Functional — `function createPlant(input)`, `function deletePlant(plant, ...)` returning new state
options.description: ADTs + pure helpers. Modern TS-idiomatic. Less ceremonial than classes; more expressive than raw types.

questions.title: Cross-context query services scaffolding
questions.context: PRD §3: "cross-context = Inngest events for async, thin read-only query services for sync reads". Example: Catalog (Phase 5) needs to read Species (Species & Care context). Phase 2 has no consumers yet.

options.label: Defer entirely — scaffold cross-context query services in their first consumer phase (Phase 5+)
options.description: Phase 2 stays focused on schema + adapters. No premature abstraction. Risk: pattern inconsistency when later phases improvise.

options.label: Scaffold one as part of smoke route (e.g., User read by Catalog from IAM context) to lock the pattern
options.description: One concrete example establishes the convention. Phase 5+ copies it. Slight extra Phase 2 scope.

options.label: Scaffold all 7 contexts' `*-queries.ts` as empty placeholders documenting the pattern
options.description: Empty stubs in `src/contexts/{ctx}/application/queries.ts` with usage examples. Establishes structure aggressively. Risk of churn when contracts emerge.

questions.title: Event type definitions in Phase 2
questions.context: PRD §3 lists every cross-context event (e.g., `user.signed_up`, `identification.succeeded`, `daily_reminder_summary.due`). Phase 2 doesn't wire Inngest, but the contract exists. Locking event payload Zod schemas now means later phases just import.

options.label: Define all event types/payload Zod schemas in `src/shared/events/` now
options.description: Locks contract early. Phase 4-8 just import. Some events may need refactoring as their payloads evolve. Most upfront design.

options.label: Per-context event types in `src/contexts/{ctx}/domain/events.ts` — context-owned
options.description: Each context owns its emitted events. Cross-context consumers import. Aligns with DDD ownership.

options.label: Defer entirely — events live in Phase 4 when Inngest lands
options.description: Phase 2 stays pure data layer. Risk: events designed in isolation per phase, no upfront contract.

questions.title: Integration test DB isolation
questions.context: PRD §19: "REAL Postgres, zero DB mocking, migrations applied as in production". Multiple Vitest workers in CI; each test needs a clean state. Choice trades speed vs purity.

options.label: Transaction-rollback per test — wrap each test in `BEGIN ... ROLLBACK`
options.description: Fastest. Breaks if code under test uses its own transactions (Drizzle nests them as savepoints — works). All tests share one DB.

options.label: TRUNCATE all tables between each test
options.description: Reliable, slower than rollback. Works regardless of code's transaction usage. Loses sequence values, may need RESET.

options.label: Separate `test_<worker>` schema per Vitest worker, fresh between files
options.description: Parallel-safe. Each worker has its own schema. Slow startup. Most isolation.

options.label: Whole separate Postgres DB per worker via Testcontainers
options.description: Maximum isolation. Slowest. Heaviest infra. Overkill if Supavisor already separates DBs in branch-DB workflow.

questions.chat_more: Keep an exit ramp documented — if you hit a test that needs a real commit, fall back to TRUNCATE for that file.

questions.title: Auth in integration tests
questions.context: Integration tests hit real route handlers that go through middleware (JWT verify). Need a way to simulate authenticated requests.

options.label: Mock AuthAdapter via `vi.mock` — fast, doesn't exercise real verify path
options.description: Tests inject a fake user. JWT path untested. Risk: real verification logic regression goes unnoticed.

options.label: Real Supabase Auth in local stack — generate JWT via `auth.signInWithPassword()` with seeded test users
options.description: Full path exercised including JWKS verify. Slower (~50-200ms per signin). Requires test user seeding.

options.label: Hybrid — most tests mock; one or two "real" auth tests verify JWKS/verify path
options.description: Speed for the bulk; coverage for the edge. Mocking convention may hide bugs in mocked tests.

questions.title: Smoke E2E coverage in Phase 2
questions.context: Phase 1 has a Playwright smoke with diagnostics routes. Phase 2 adds backend logic. Question: does Phase 2 add new Playwright coverage or stay in Vitest?

options.label: Phase 2 adds Playwright spec covering the smoke `/api/v1/...` route — verifies JWT + cursor + idempotency end-to-end via real HTTP
options.description: Visible end-to-end. Real Next 16 build serving the route. Most confidence.

options.label: Smoke testing lives in Vitest integration only; Playwright deferred to feature phases
options.description: Vitest covers the route handler imported as a function. Faster CI. Playwright ramps up in Phase 5+ with UI.

options.label: Both — Vitest integration is primary, one Playwright happy-path smoke
options.description: Belt-and-suspenders. Slight redundancy. Higher CI time.

questions.title: User row schema fill-out at Phase 2
questions.context: PRD §4 lists 11 User fields (id, email, name, locale, timezone, notification_time_local, trial_source, partner_code, age_confirmed_at, toxicity_disclaimer_acknowledged_at, deletion_requested_at, created_at). Phase 4 wires auth/signup, Phase 8 wires reminders, Phase 11 wires deletion. Question: how much of the User table ships in Phase 2?

options.label: Full schema per PRD §4 — all 11 fields with sensible defaults; Phase 4+ adds the wire-up logic
options.description: Single migration sets the table. Subsequent phases just write to existing columns. Minimum migration churn.

options.label: Minimum viable — id, email, created_at; other columns added per migration as their phase needs them
options.description: Each phase explicitly evolves the schema. Migration churn but clear lineage. Risk: many small migrations to coordinate.

options.label: Full schema + sync stub (DB trigger or app-side) defined but not wired to actual auth flow
options.description: Closer to production-ready. Phase 4 just turns it on. Some Phase 4 logic leaks into Phase 2.

questions.title: JWT verification posture for Phase 2 smoke route
questions.context: Phase 2 SC-4 says "enforces JWT verification". But Phase 4 owns auth. Question: does the smoke route require a real JWT (operator generates manually) or stay public for now?

options.label: Smoke route requires real JWT (401 if missing) — proves middleware/adapter end-to-end
options.description: Strict to SC-4 wording. Operators/integration tests generate JWTs against local Supabase auth. Most realistic.

options.label: Smoke route public — Phase 4 turns on JWT enforcement
options.description: Easier Phase 2 testing. Strict reading of SC-4 violated unless it's interpreted as "middleware exists, route opts in".

options.label: Smoke route public + a separate `/api/v1/_authcheck` route requires JWT — both postures covered
options.description: SC-4 satisfied (some route enforces JWT). Smoke tests can hit the public route without auth dance. Two routes.

questions.title: ConsentLog seed strategy (INFRA-24 specifics)
questions.context: INFRA-24 says "ConsentLog, policy_version, legal-basis registry seed data loaded". "Policy_version" is on every ConsentLog row referencing the active T&C/privacy version. "Legal-basis registry" enumerates Art. 7 bases: contract, consent, legitimate_interest, etc. Question: what shape do these take?

options.label: Static seed: legal_basis registry as a `legal_basis_registry` table (purpose enum → legal_basis enum) + initial `policy_version='v1.0.0'` row in a `policy_versions` table
options.description: Two reference tables seeded. ConsentLog references via FK. Clear separation. Phase 4+ writes ConsentLog rows pointing to these registries.

options.label: No registry tables — `policy_version` is a varchar on ConsentLog (default 'v1.0.0' from env), `legal_basis` is a varchar with CHECK or enum
options.description: Less ceremonial. No FK joins. Registry exists only in code (TS const). Risk: drift between DB and TS.

options.label: Hybrid — `legal_basis` as PG enum (registry) + `policy_version` as a single `policy_versions` table with `is_current` flag
options.description: Enums for closed sets, table for evolving versions. Phase 4 re-consent flow can mark a new version as current. Most flexible.

questions.chat_more: Most operational statuses should stay varchar + CHECK for easier evolution. legal_basis can be a PG enum because it is a legally closed registry; document that exception.

questions.title: Provider config seed (IdentificationLimit + ProviderBudget) timing
questions.context: Phase 6 (Identification) is when caps actually engage. PRD §6 lists defaults: trial 5/day + 75/period, paid 15/day + 200/period; Plant.id $5/day, OpenAI-compat $5/day, alert 80%, min_confidence 0.30.

options.label: Seed defaults in Phase 2 — `IdentificationLimit` rows for trial + paid; `ProviderBudget` rows for Plant.id + OpenAI-compat (identification + care_guide purposes)
options.description: A fresh DB is identification-ready when Phase 6 lands. Aligns with INFRA-05 ("all entities exist"). Slight Phase 2 scope creep but minimal.

options.label: Seed only the schema (empty tables); Phase 6 seeds defaults
options.description: Strict Phase 2 boundary. Phase 6 must remember to seed before tests.

options.label: Seed empty tables + ship a `pnpm db:seed:providers` operator script Phase 6 invokes
options.description: Convention without commitment. Operator/CI invokes when needed. Slightly hedged.
